text: Robin Roberts, born November 23, 1960, is an American television broadcaster who co-anchors ABC's Good Morning America. She was born in Tuskegee, Alabama, and grew up in Pass Christian, Mississippi, where she played basketball and tennis and graduated as the salutatorian of Pass Christian High School in 1979. She is the daughter of Lucimarian (née Tolliver) and Colonel Lawrence E. Roberts, a Tuskegee Airman, and is the youngest of four siblings, following Sally-Ann, Lawrence Jr. (nicknamed Butch), and Dorothy. Roberts attended Southeastern Louisiana University in Hammond, Louisiana, graduating cum laude in 1983 with a degree in communication, where she was a standout on the women's basketball team, ending her career as the school's third all-time leading scorer with 1,446 points and 1,034 rebounds—making her one of only three Lady Lions to reach 1,000 points and 1,000 rebounds. During her senior season, she averaged 27.6 points per game, and her jersey number 21 was retired by Southeastern on February 5, 2011. She began her career in 1983 as a sports anchor and reporter for WDAM-TV in Hattiesburg, Mississippi, then moved to WLOX-TV in Biloxi in 1984, WSMV-TV in Nashville in 1986, and WAGA-TV in Atlanta from 1988 to 1990, where she also hosted on radio station V-103. In February 1990, she joined ESPN as a sportscaster, working there until 2005, during which time she co-hosted NFL Primetime and used the catchphrase "Go on with your bad self!" She began working for ABC News as a featured reporter on Good Morning America in June 1995 and hosted ABC's Wide World of Sports from 1996 to 1998. In 2005, she was promoted to co-anchor of Good Morning America. After Diane Sawyer left in December 2009, George Stephanopoulos joined her as co-anchor, and their partnership led the program back to number one in the ratings by April 2012, surpassing NBC's Today, which had held the top spot for 16 years. In the fall of 2005, Roberts anchored emotional reports from the Mississippi Gulf Coast following Hurricane Katrina, which severely impacted her hometown of Pass Christian, where her high school was reduced to rubble. She hosted the Academy Awards preshow for ABC on February 22, 2009, and again in 2011. In 2010, she guest-starred on Disney Channel's Hannah Montana in season 4, episode 10, "Can You See the Real Me?", and drove the Pace Car for the 2010 Indianapolis 500 on May 30, 2010. In 2012, she was inducted into the Women's Basketball Hall of Fame for her contributions to women's basketball through broadcasting and play. In 2014, she was named one of ESPNW's Impact 25 and founded Rock'n Robin Productions. She executive-produced and narrated the documentary Tuskegee Airmen: Legacy of Courage, which premiered on History on February 10, 2021. Roberts is Presbyterian and practices Transcendental Meditation. In 2005, she began a romantic relationship with massage therapist Amber Laign, which she publicly acknowledged in late December 2013, and they married in September 2023. In 2007, she was diagnosed with early breast cancer, underwent surgery on August 3, and completed eight chemotherapy treatments by January 2008. In 2012, she was diagnosed with myelodysplastic syndrome (MDS), a bone marrow disease, which led to a 1,800 percent spike in bone marrow donors for Be the Match Registry on the day she went public with her illness. She took a leave from GMA to undergo a bone marrow transplant, returning to the show on February 20, 2013, after going home in October 2012. Her coverage of her MDS diagnosis earned her a 2012 Peabody Award for allowing her network to document her battle and inspire hundreds of potential donors to register, raising awareness of the need for more bone marrow donors. ESPN awarded her the Arthur Ashe Courage Award at the 2013 ESPYs, and the NBA honored her with the Sager Strong Award at its June 20, 2019, ceremony. On May 19, 2018, she co-anchored the wedding of Prince Harry and Meghan Markle at St. George's Chapel in Windsor. In 2021, she served as a guest host on Jeopardy! for five episodes from July 19 to 23, following Alex Trebek's death in November 2020, and launched the Disney+ interview series Turning the Tables with Robin Roberts. She also performed as a backup singer in the film Pitch Perfect 2. On October 10, 2018, she was selected as a mentor for Disney's #DreamBigPrincess campaign.
